title: Intrinsic affine-local flatness implies exact sheaf tensor
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and G a quasi-coherent structure-sheaf module [pqf-def-coherent]. If IsFlatOver G (identity Y) [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] holds, then G is tensor-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]: the functor tensorRight G on structure-sheaf modules is exact.

proof.text: Specialize IsFlatOver G (identity Y) at equal affine opens V=U. Apply flat_stalk_of_affine_sections_flat to obtain Module.Flat O_Y,x G_x for every point x.

The module stalk functor preserves finite limits: after forgetting to abelian groups it is the composite of the module-to-sheaf functor with the exact abelian-sheaf stalk functor. Reflect finite-limit preservation through the module-to-abelian-group forgetful functor. The family of module stalk functors jointly reflects isomorphisms by the abelian-sheaf stalk isomorphism criterion.

Use stalkTensorIso, natural in both arguments, to identify tensorRight G followed by the stalk at x with the stalk followed by tensorRight G_x. Module.Flat.iff_preservesFiniteLimits_tensorRight supplies finite-limit preservation for the latter. Joint reflection of limits by the stalk functors then gives finite-limit preservation for tensorRight G.

The upstream SheafOfModules.monoidalClosed construction makes tensorLeft G a left adjoint, hence it preserves finite colimits. Symmetry transfers this to tensorRight G. Together with the finite-limit preservation just proved, this is precisely SheafOfModules.IsFlat G.
